findings.observation: Resource adapters cannot import action-owned contracts under the current allowlist. Composition can import both and implements intermediate translation.
findings.decision: Permit resources to implement their consumer action contracts directly, without executing actions; continue banning action imports of resources/Tableau and action-to-action dependencies.
findings.alternative: Colocate concrete adapters with actions, but that couples the entire Go workflow package to provider packages without removing required normalization behavior.
findings.preserve: Fail-closed import enforcement, meaningful lower-level boundaries, explicit narrow ports, and no cycles.
findings.verification: Replace exact import fixtures through an approved architecture change; demonstrate allowed consumer-port imports and rejected reverse/CLI/HTTP dependencies. No gate changes made now.

findings.observation: Shared app inventory code combines bounded native collection, cache publication policy, and six resource-specific action page adapters.
findings.decision: Create internal/inventory for action-neutral collection/publication orchestration; retain typed readers with existing resource adapters and native collection in tableau/cache.
findings.preserve: Partial inventory never replaces complete cache scope; filtered results upsert rather than replace; exact target scope, stable order, freshness evidence, and existing bounds survive.
findings.verification: Map inventory snapshot compatibility, cache staging, partial coverage, filter parity, and list result tests before extraction. Existing tests are not all semantically audited.

findings.observation: Composition owns accepted-write receipt persistence, monitoring, resource completion, detached-worker dispatch, and later recovery reconciliation.
findings.decision: Extend existing jobmonitor and operationrun mechanism owners with injected observers; move typed resource completion to resource workflows/adapters and user recovery to actions/job. App retains process dispatch only.
findings.preserve: Native job identity is not worker identity; accepted writes survive cancellation; monitoring cannot resubmit writes; exact site and destination verification remain explicit.
findings.verification: Detailed state-machine characterization and shared-consumer tests are prerequisites for this high-risk slice; symbol-level role mapping is not runtime proof.

findings.observation: Invocation-scoped setup reuses configuration, sessions, transports, clients, workspaces, and discovery paths. Comments distinguish setup snapshots from mutation validation evidence.
findings.decision: Keep construction and lifetime ownership in app while removing per-operation facades; move phase forwarding into the substantive project adapter.
findings.preserve: No new connection per batch item, no cached mutation observation substituted for fresh validation, no process-global user/runtime state.
findings.verification: Retain session sharing, phase read counts, cancellation/cleanup, target isolation, and constructor-only startup behavior.

findings.observation: Command facts live partly in global help switches and examples. Catalog-mounted lineage and labels are constructed from content CLI code.
findings.decision: Colocate resource help/flag metadata with command constructors, keep common rendering in CLI, and move catalog-mounted command construction into cli/catalog without changing public routes.
findings.preserve: Existing help/output syntax, aliases, flags/defaults, capability bindings, parsing, preview policy, and batch controls.
findings.verification: Compare registered command trees, help fixtures, aliases, capability bindings, and invalid-input behavior. Do not regenerate goldens merely to accept drift.

findings.observation: Result capture, batch parsing, and capability metadata serve different responsibilities despite crossing many commands.
findings.decision: Retain separate output/lastcommand, CLI/contentbatch, and capability owners; move reusable capture coordination through injected snapshots rather than merging everything into a runtime utility package.
findings.preserve: Actual user outcome survives saved-result failure, mixed batch outcomes remain ordered, and discovery/readiness remains distinct from executable command syntax.
findings.verification: Shared contracts require affected-consumer checks across categories; app.Run integration stays at the process boundary.

findings.observation: The human contribution entry point delegates detailed engineering guidance to a skill; generated references consume capability metadata.
findings.decision: Add a human-readable architecture/navigation guide and repeatable resource addition walkthrough, linked from CONTRIBUTING; align agent guidance and regenerate generated references through their tools.
findings.preserve: One maintained architecture, no competing hidden instructions, no manually edited generated artifacts, and no claim of Tableau endorsement.
findings.verification: Cold-maintainer navigation exercises use content, administration, Pulse, and local-state commands; no coaching or reliance on historical review phases.

limits: Structural recommendations are concrete but not approved implementation instructions.
No tests, native fixture operations, installed CLI commands, source checkout, pushes, or external mutations ran.
No claim of exhaustive test audit or complete worker/recovery state-machine review.
The package decision map deliberately retains meaningful infrastructure even where detailed implementation review remains pending.
Existing pilot test-effectiveness gaps and correctness hypotheses remain separate from structural consolidation.
